_meta.purpose: Per-symbol-set bias rules for BCI classification quality scoring
_meta.source: Derived from bci-symbol-map.csv (6490 concepts × 6 sets) + 80 classification samples
_meta.usage: aacResolver reads these rules to score/filter symbol matches per set before rendering AacCards

strengths: 1:1 mapping to BCI — every concept has exactly one Bliss symbol
No search bias — symbols are generated from BCI codes, not keyword search
Grammar indicators built in (tense, plural, comparative etc)
Consistent visual language across all concepts
weaknesses: Abstract visual system — not intuitive without training
No photorealistic depiction — all geometric/schematic
Requires Bliss literacy to interpret
bliss.notes: Bliss is the reference set — no bias correction needed. Every BCI concept has a Bliss symbol by definition.

strengths: Concrete nouns generally good (apple, bicycle, bell)
weaknesses: Keyword search returns wrong homonym sense frequently
Substring matching produces catastrophic mismatches
Multi-language corpus causes cross-language bleed
Falls back to deterministic garbage for unknown terms

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC keyword search matches substrings, returning wrong homonym

examples.reason: 'run' matched the piste not the action

bias_rules.detection: If ARASAAC image filename contains words not in the BCI glosses, flag as suspect

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC multi-language corpus returns results from wrong language

examples.reason: matched compound phrase not core concept

bias_rules.detection: If ARASAAC result contains non-English words or prefixes (tu, le, la, de, el, das, het), flag

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC matches the right root word but wrong verbal sense or context

examples.reason: correct — but CSV shows it matched correctly here

bias_rules.detection: If ARASAAC image filename contains a phrase (2+ words) where the BCI gloss is a single word, flag as wrong sense

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC returns the same garbage image for all unrecognised terms
bias_rules.detection: If multiple unrelated words resolve to the same ARASAAC image, it's a fallback. Blocklist: 'bald 1', 'simple'

bias_rules.description: Keyword match returns medically/socially inappropriate image for AAC context

examples.reason: matched make substring to sexual content

bias_rules.detection: Manual review required — flag any ARASAAC result containing: intrauterine, contraceptive, sexual, genital, rectal

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC image depicts multiple concepts merged into one pictogram

examples.reason: negation shown only in specific context
wrong concept entirely — matched secondary gloss?

bias_rules.detection: If ARASAAC filename contains ' - ' separators or 3+ words, likely a merged concept

bias_rules.description: ARASAAC verbs are named with "to" prefix — search "to [verb]" for better results
bias_rules.detection: For RED (verb) POS: prepend "to" to search term when searching ARASAAC

arasaac.fallback_pattern: Returns first result from keyword search — often wrong for abstract/compound terms

weaknesses: Smallest useful coverage of the pictogram sets
Catastrophic mismatches on abstract/verb concepts
Appears to use unrelated keyword expansion
Country flags leak into results via 'country The...' pattern

bias_rules.description: Mulberry returns completely unrelated nouns for abstract verbs and function words

examples.reason: skull for help — dangerous inversion of meaning
close but oddly specific gendered image

bias_rules.detection: For RED (verb) and WHITE (function) POS: always cross-check Mulberry result against BCI glosses. If zero gloss words appear in Mulberry filename, reject.

bias_rules.description: Mulberry returns country flags/names via 'country The...' pattern
bias_rules.detection: If Mulberry filename starts with 'country ', reject

bias_rules.description: Mulberry matched a secondary BCI gloss instead of the primary concept

examples.reason: matched the letter W not the pronoun

bias_rules.detection: If Mulberry filename is a compound where only part matches a BCI gloss, downgrade

bias_rules.description: Mulberry shows a complex scene instead of the core concept

examples.reason: showed AAC device not the act of chatting

bias_rules.detection: If Mulberry filename contains 3+ words describing a scene, it's probably not the core concept

mulberry.fallback_pattern: Returns seemingly random concrete noun when keyword has no match

strengths: Good for concrete nouns and actions with clear visual
weaknesses: Shows complex multi-step SCENES instead of single concepts
Verb results often show entire activity sequences
Abstract concepts get wildly wrong visual metaphors
Filename often describes a sentence not a word

bias_rules.description: Sclera shows a complex scene or activity sequence instead of a single concept

examples.reason: showed shutting pants instead of generic 'close'
entire action sequence: person + bicycle + shed

examples.got: put the dishes in the cupboard
examples.reason: entire sentence for a definite article
showed a notice/sign, not a building

bias_rules.detection: If Sclera filename contains 4+ words, it's a scene description not a concept. Reject for single-word resolution.

bias_rules.description: Sclera matched a different meaning of a homonym word

examples.reason: matched 'wave' as ring shape not ocean/hand
rocket for boat/ship — possibly matched 'ship' as spaceship?

bias_rules.detection: Cross-check Sclera result against primary BCI gloss. If result is a different semantic domain, reject.

bias_rules.description: Sclera shows the concept embedded in a specific activity rather than in isolation

examples.reason: two-step instruction, not the concept of remembering
matched 'act' gloss but as 'act silly' specifically

bias_rules.detection: If Sclera filename contains a verb + preposition/object that narrows the BCI concept, downgrade

sclera.fallback_pattern: Returns complex scene descriptions — treats search term as sentence context not isolated concept

strengths: Good for concrete nouns and UI concepts
weaknesses: Icons only — no verb or action depictions
No pictographic context (just silhouettes)
Cannot represent abstract concepts visually
Lowest overlap with AAC vocabulary needs

bias_rules.description: Noun Project is icon-focused — verb concepts get a generic icon that doesn't convey the action
examples: All RED (verb) POS entries get a noun icon — e.g. 'run' might get a running shoe icon, not the action of running
bias_rules.detection: For BCI POS = RED, always prefer ARASAAC or Bliss over Noun Project

bias_rules.description: Noun Project cannot depict function words (the, not, what, who, at, for, but)
examples: WHITE POS entries (function words) have no meaningful icon representation
bias_rules.detection: For BCI POS = WHITE or BLUE, reject Noun Project entirely

noun_project.fallback_pattern: Returns closest icon by keyword — reasonable for nouns, useless for verbs/function words

strengths: Arabic-world cultural context (useful for Arabic-speaking AAC users)
Pictograms designed for AAC use specifically
weaknesses: Lowest coverage (37%) — huge vocabulary gaps
Western-biased BCI concepts may not map to Tawasol cultural concepts
Limited utility as primary set for English-language AAC

bias_rules.description: Tawasol only covers 37% of BCI concepts — always need a fallback set
bias_rules.detection: If no Tawasol match exists, fall through to next set in priority. Never block on Tawasol absence.

tawasol.fallback_pattern: Sparse coverage — most concepts have no Tawasol match

strengths: Excellent for emotions, food, animals, objects
Consistent art style across all symbols
High imageability — designed for instant recognition
weaknesses: Limited to emoji vocabulary — no verbs, prepositions, or grammar concepts
Cultural context may not match AAC needs (e.g. emoji for sarcasm)
Small set (2,770) relative to ARASAAC or Noun Project
No action/scene depictions — single object only

bias_rules.description: Twemoji has no verb or action representations — only objects and faces
bias_rules.detection: For BCI POS = RED (verb), reject Twemoji entirely

bias_rules.description: Twemoji cannot depict function words, pronouns, or grammar concepts
bias_rules.detection: For BCI POS = WHITE, BLUE, reject Twemoji entirely

twemoji.fallback_pattern: Returns emoji-style pictogram if keyword matches — good for concrete nouns and emotions

strengths: Good for UI concepts and simple objects
weaknesses: Very small set (907 symbols)
Icon-focused — no scene or action depictions
Monochrome only — limited visual distinction between concepts
Mixed licensing — some icons may not be freely usable

bias_rules.description: IcoMoon icons are UI-style — may not communicate AAC concepts clearly
bias_rules.detection: Prefer ARASAAC or Mulberry pictograms over IcoMoon icons for AAC use

icomoon.fallback_pattern: Returns monochrome icon — reasonable for nouns, poor for everything else

weaknesses: Very small set (600 symbols)
Inconsistent art styles — aggregated from multiple sources
Mixed licensing complicates reuse
Not designed for AAC — general-purpose icon collection

bias_rules.description: IconArchive aggregates multiple art styles — inconsistent visual language
bias_rules.detection: Prefer sets with consistent style (ARASAAC, Mulberry, Twemoji) over IconArchive

icon_archive.fallback_pattern: Returns detailed colourful icon — good quality but inconsistent style

weaknesses: Tiny set (205 symbols) — massive vocabulary gaps
Non-commercial licence limits some uses
Very limited coverage — only useful as occasional fallback

bias_rules.description: LanguageCraft only covers 205 concepts — always need a fallback set
bias_rules.detection: If no LanguageCraft match exists, fall through. Never block on absence.

language_craft.fallback_pattern: Sparse coverage — most concepts have no match

weaknesses: Extremely small set (21 symbols)
Essentially negligible for general use

resolution_priority.description: Per-set priority order for resolving a BCI concept to a symbol image

order.trust: high for YELLOW nouns, low for RED verbs and WHITE function words
high for YELLOW nouns, reject for RED/WHITE/BLUE
medium for YELLOW nouns only — scene bias makes verbs unusable
medium for YELLOW only — icon style, no verbs
medium where available, coverage gaps expected

order.when: emoji-style preferred or concrete noun fallback
order.trust: high for YELLOW nouns and GREEN adjectives, reject for RED/WHITE/BLUE
low — UI icon style not AAC pictogram

pos_trust_matrix.description: Which sets to trust per POS colour. 'trust' = use as-is, 'check' = verify against glosses, 'reject' = never use

gloss_match_scoring.description: How to score a symbol set result against BCI glosses

compound_word_rules.description: How to handle hyphenated Phosphor icon names (e.g. airplane-taxiing, align-center-horizontal)
rules: Split on hyphens, try each segment against BCI glosses
If only one segment matches, the match is LOW confidence
If the compound contains 'logo', 'simple', 'fill', 'bold' — it's a UI variant, not an AAC concept
Compounds with 3+ segments are almost never AAC-resolvable

homonym_resolution.description: BCI has 238 homonyms (same primary gloss, different concepts). Rules for disambiguation.
rules: Prefer the concept whose secondary glosses narrow the sense (e.g. 'bar,pub' vs 'bar,cake')
If context_overrides table has a rule for this word in this context, use it
If POS is known from sentence context, prefer the concept with matching POS
If no disambiguation possible, prefer the lower BCI index (older = more core concept)

deprecated_concept_rules.description: 156 BCI concepts are marked (OLD) — deprecated in the registry
rules: If a concept has (OLD) suffix, check if a non-OLD concept exists with same primary gloss
Prefer non-OLD over OLD when both exist
If only OLD exists (e.g. remember-(to)_(OLD)), use it but flag for manual review

numbered_variant_fallback.description: When visual verification fails, try searching with postfix number
rules: ARASAAC uses numbered variants: walk, walk 1, walk 2, to walk 1, to walk 2
Tawasol uses gendered variants: walk (F), walk (M)
If first result fails visual check, try "[term] 1", "[term] 2" etc.
Numbered variants often show different depictions of same concept (e.g. baby vs adult walking)
Cannot distinguish variants from text alone — visual verification required

url_name_mismatch.description: Detect when API result name and image URL filename disagree
rules: Extract filename from image URL (e.g. mitten.png from .../mitten.png)
If filename shares no words with the result name, flag as url_name_mismatch
Example: result named "want" but URL is mitten.png — ARASAAC served wrong image
This catches API-level errors that text matching alone cannot detect

content_blocklist.description: Result names containing these phrases are rejected across ALL sets
